explanations: Yes. worker() calls p.wg.Add(1) from inside the goroutine, so the WaitGroup counter is incremented only once the scheduler runs that goroutine. If Shutdown() is called soon after Start(), wg.Wait() can observe a zero counter and return before any worker has registered; Shutdown then closes p.results while workers are still starting and draining jobs, and a worker's send on the closed channel panics (and queued rides are not processed). wg.Add must happen in Start() before each `go` statement.
The select with a default case makes the send non-blocking, so a full channel yields ErrQueueFull right away. Nothing blocks, nothing is evicted, and the pool never grows beyond its fixed size.

A closed buffered channel still delivers its remaining items to receivers; `for req := range p.jobs` exits only after the buffer is empty. ErrClosed is only returned from Submit calls made after the closed flag is set, and no further Submit is needed.

The timeout only works if FindDriver honors ctx; a call that ignores it holds its worker forever. With every worker occupied nothing drains the queue, so it fills and Submit sheds load. The pool is fixed-size and Shutdown would wait on wg for those stuck workers rather than return early.
